attempted_claim: Let A be an infinite-dimensional, unital, separable, simple, nuclear C*-algebra in the UCT class with TR(A)=0. Let alpha in Aut(A) have the Osaka-Phillips tracial Rokhlin property: for every finite F subset A, epsilon>0, n in N, and nonzero x in A_+, there are mutually orthogonal projections e_0,...,e_n such that ||alpha(e_j)-e_{j+1}||<epsilon for 0<=j<n, ||[e_j,a]||<epsilon for every a in F, and [1-sum_{j=0}^n e_j] is Cuntz subequivalent to x. Must TR(A crossed product_alpha Z)=0 hold, without assuming the stronger tracially cyclic Rokhlin condition ||alpha(e_n)-e_0||<epsilon or that some power alpha^r is approximately inner?
decisive_failure: No proof or disproof of the admitted target is offered: the YES-proof fails on the wrap-around norm obstruction without the excluded cyclic or approximately-inner hypotheses, and no verified counterexample with certified TR-jump was constructed. The verified non-cyclic consequences (real rank zero, stable rank one, order determined by traces) are documented but provably insufficient for TR0. The tower-defect script is a routine illustration of the known proof gap, not evidence for any original claim.
